penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Per-repo onboarding requires identifying which modules are 'high-risk zones' (payments, auth) in each customer's codebase — a human configuration and calibration step that cannot be fully automated without customer involvement.

penalties_applied.name: high_touch_support
penalties_applied.reason: False positives and missed catches in security-critical code paths will generate high-anxiety, human-judgement support requests from engineering leads.

rationale: The pain is severe and well-evidenced (47-comment thread, recurring industry pattern), and the buyer — tech leads at AI-assisted startups — does pay for code quality tooling. However, a credible AI-diff review layer for payment and auth code requires per-repo configuration to identify sensitive zones, which is inherently manual per-customer work. Operational autonomy scores 5, well below the build gate floor of 7, and the heavy onboarding drops the total to 3.9 after penalties.
solution_plan: Not viable in current form for a solo non-technical operator. The core value proposition — targeted review of AI-generated diffs in high-risk code paths — requires integrating with each customer's CI/CD pipeline and tagging their specific sensitive modules. That onboarding is not automatable via Claude + a form. A stripped-down version (e.g. a GitHub Action that sends AI-generated diffs to Claude for a generic security review) could be an open-source project but is unlikely to generate subscription revenue without the custom-zone intelligence that makes it trustworthy.
notes: Fails operational_autonomy_min (5 < 7) build gate. Total also drops to 3.9 after penalties, below validate threshold.
